ben_customer: Hey team — after upgrading our app's redwood Python SDK from 1.11.3 -> 1.12.0 I'm getting an exception on startup: TypeError: Unexpected keyword argument 'credentials'.
jen_support: Thanks for the report, Ben. Can you paste the exact pip package and the snippet where you instantiate the client?
ben_customer: Sure — Dockerfile snippet and quick traceback: ```
RUN pip install redwood-sdk==1.12.0

Traceback (most recent call last):
  File \"app.py\", line 12, in <module>
    client = RedwoodClient(credentials=env_creds)
TypeError: __init__() got an unexpected keyword argument 'credentials'
```
clara_devex: Hmm — that sounds like a breaking change in the client constructor. Do you also have any pinned transitive deps (e.g., redwood-core) in your env? Can you share `pip freeze` output?
ben_customer: pip freeze: ```
redwood-sdk==1.12.0
redwood-core==0.9.1
requests==2.31.0
```
jen_support: OK — two immediate suggestions: 1) Workaround: pin back to the last known-good SDK for your app until we confirm the change: `pip install redwood-sdk==1.11.3 --force-reinstall` (or add `redwood-sdk==1.11.3` to requirements.txt). 2) Short repro: try `python -c \"from redwood import RedwoodClient; print(RedwoodClient.__init__.__code__.co_varnames)\"` to see current ctor args.
ben_customer: Pinning to 1.11.3 fixed it for now, thanks. Would like to know if this was intentional.
dan_engineering: Thanks for the ping — I'll dig in. Quick context: v1.12.0 removed the legacy `credentials=` kwarg in favor of the unified `auth=` object (we documented in the changelog but I realize that may not have been highlighted). That caused the TypeError.
clara_devex: Got it. Can you check if the changelog and release notes were missing the migration snippet? We should provide a short compatibility blurb and example: ```
# old
client = RedwoodClient(credentials=Credentials.from_env())
# new
client = RedwoodClient(auth=Credentials.from_env())
```
dan_engineering: Will do. Also looking at why `redwood-core` mismatch might make this surface (some installs pick up old wheels). I'll open a ticket to add a deprecation alias in a patch release so existing installs don't break: RD-ISSUE-4521.
infra-bot: Ticket created: RD-ISSUE-4521 — "Add backward-compatible alias for deprecated credentials kwarg in Python SDK" — assigned to @dan_engineering.
jen_support: For support notes: recommend telling customers to pin to `redwood-sdk==1.11.3` if they cannot migrate immediately, and give the one-line migration example above. Also advise clearing caches if `pip` shows mixed versions: `pip cache purge` then reinstall.
ben_customer: Appreciate the guidance. ETA on the patch?
dan_engineering: I'll try to get a 1.12.1 hotfix out today that reintroduces a kwarg alias with a deprecation warning. If you need faster, stick with 1.11.3.
clara_devex: I'll prepare a short snippet and update the release notes + changelog to include the migration example and a clear deprecation window. :thumbsup:
ben_customer: Thanks everyone — pin + plan to migrate to `auth=` when patch available.
jen_support: Marking as resolved on our side for now; re-open if you see anything after the hotfix. :white_check_mark:
